title: What Forma is for
summary: One coach for training, food and progress.
text: forma is a coach you talk to. open the app and speak or type on one coach screen. ask for a session, log a meal, add a weigh-in, or look back at your progress. you do not need to learn a set of screens before you begin. start with something ordinary, such as log breakfast 107 g cucumber or start training . what the coach can help with training: start a session, warm up, cool down, or fit training around the time you have. food: log what you ate and see your calorie and protein targets. your body: record your weight and look at body trends. recovery: ask about sleep, heart-rate variability and resting heart rate. progress: check a lift, new records, training volume and your week. train, fuel and reports are still there when you want a full screen. open the grid menu at the top right of the coach screen and choose one. a quiet view of today the home screen has a strip of six numbers: this week, protein, weight, sleep, hrv and resting heart rate. tap a number to open its chart. the morning check-in lets you say how you feel. choose wrecked, flat, normal, good or strong, or say something like i feel 7 . an optional morning nudge can help you start the day. your information stays yours speech is recognised on your iphone and is never sent anywhere. forma core keeps everything on your phone. icloud backup uses your own private icloud. forma power is optional. it adds garmin data and online ai help for free-form questions, meal ideas, meal photos and meal descriptions. you choose whether to turn online ai help on. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. forma gives information, not medical advice. related one coach, one menu setting up talk to your coach privacy: what stays where

title: One coach, one menu
summary: Find your way around the coach screen, grid menu and home numbers.
text: forma opens on one coach screen. talk or type there for most things. the grid menu at the top right opens train, fuel and reports when you want to look closer. the coach screen use the coach screen for everyday requests. you can say or type things like: log espresso i weigh 78.4 start training how did i sleep this week how was my week the same screen is also the place to ask what can you do when you want a reminder of what forma understands. the grid menu open the grid at the top right, then choose: train for your training view. fuel for your food and targets. reports for a coach summary and your progress. reports starts with a short coach summary and an on-track card. the card brings together your fitness score, weight, muscle progress and body trends. choose full report to open the full progress screen. the six home numbers a quiet strip on the home screen shows this week, protein, weight, sleep, hrv and resting heart rate. tap one to see its chart. you can also ask the coach about these numbers in your own words. settings, backup and memories settings is where you can manage your data. export and delete options are under data & backup . to review the few things the coach remembers, open settings , then data & backup , then what the coach remembers . related what forma is for reports and the numbers on your home screen what your coach remembers

title: Setting up
summary: Your first conversation, your targets and your first session.
text: the first run is a conversation with your coach. answer a few basic questions in your own time. there is no separate setup maze to work through. what the coach asks the conversation covers: your name; your goal; your height and weight; your sex and birth date; how many days you want to train; where you train. these answers give forma a starting point for your targets and training. give the answers that apply to you. if you are unsure about your training week, choose a number of days you can realistically keep. the reveal at the end the conversation ends with your starting plan. forma reveals: your calorie target; your protein target; your first session. read them before you move on. this is the beginning of the plan, not a test you have to pass. your first conversation after setup you can keep using the same coach screen. try start training when you are ready for the first session, or log something simple such as log espresso . you do not have to use every feature on day one. a check-in, one meal and one training session are enough to begin. privacy from the start forma core works on your phone. speech is recognised on the iphone and is never sent anywhere. your icloud backup, if you use it, belongs to your own private icloud. apple health is optional and read-only. forma power and its online ai help are optional too. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. note: calorie and protein targets are estimates. forma gives information, not medical advice. related your first week core and power voice and privacy

title: Your first week
summary: A gentle seven-day start with no pressure to log everything perfectly.
text: your first week is for learning how you like to use forma. speak when that is easiest. type when you are somewhere quiet. keep the requests small. day one: meet your coach finish the first conversation about your goal, body details and training week. look at the calorie and protein targets and the first session that forma reveals. then try one everyday request, such as log espresso or i weigh 78.4 . day two: try the morning check-in choose the word that fits: wrecked, flat, normal, good or strong. if a number is easier, say i feel 7 . be honest rather than hopeful. the check-in is for you and your coach, not a score to win. day three: log a meal your way say or type what you ate. for example, log breakfast 107 g cucumber . open fuel from the grid menu if you want to see the food view. you do not need to open it every time you log something. day four: train or move a little if it is a training day, say start training . ask for warm up first if you want one. if time is tight, say i only have 35 minutes . on a non-training day, desk reset or stretch can be a small way to break up sitting. day five: ask about a number tap one of the six home numbers for its chart. or ask how did i sleep this week or resting heart rate this month . a single number is only a snapshot. give yourself time to build a trend. day six: look at training progress after you have some training history, try show my bench progress , any new records or show my training volume . early on, there may not be much to show. that is normal. day seven: review the week ask how was my week or am i on track . then open reports from the grid menu for the short coach summary and on-track card. notice what felt easy. keep that part for next week. you do not need a perfect logging streak to make forma useful. related setting up talk to your coach morning check-in and nudges reports and the numbers on your home screen

title: A day with Forma
summary: A light daily rhythm built around a few short conversations.
text: there is no long daily checklist. tell the coach what happened, ask what you need, and get on with your day. in the morning check in if you want to. choose wrecked, flat, normal, good or strong. you can also say i feel 7 . if you use the optional morning nudge, it can give you a gentle prompt for the day. then glance at the six home numbers if you want a quick view of sleep, hrv, resting heart rate and the rest. when you eat tell the coach what you had. keep it as simple as you like: log breakfast 107 g cucumber log espresso open fuel from the grid menu when you want the fuller food view. when you train say start training . you can add context before you begin: i only have 35 minutes equipment taken? warm up when you finish, ask for cool down or stretch if that would feel good. when you want to check in ask one question instead of digging through charts: am i on track show my bench progress how did i sleep this week how was my week open reports from the grid menu for the coach summary and the wider picture. tip: a missed day does not need a big reset. open forma and tell the coach the next true thing, such as i weigh 78.4 or log my creatine . related your first week morning check-in and nudges short on time reports and the numbers on your home screen

title: Core and Power
summary: What stays on your phone and what the optional Power plan adds.
text: forma has two plans: forma core and forma power. both use the same coach-first app. the difference is whether you want garmin data and optional online ai help. forma core core is everything on your phone. you can talk or type to the coach, log food and weight, train, check in, and see your reports and charts. speech recognition happens on the iphone. your coach memories stay on the phone too. backup goes to your own private icloud. apple health is optional. forma only reads from it; it does not write to it. forma power power adds: garmin data for the watch information forma can use. free-form questions with online ai help. meal ideas with online ai help. meal photos and descriptions that online ai can help interpret. online ai help is opt-in. you choose whether to use it. the watch-data boundary nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. that boundary applies even when you use power and turn online ai help on. this is separate from choosing to send a free-form question, meal idea request, meal photo or meal description for online ai help. which one should you use? choose core if you want the coach and your data on your phone without online ai help. consider power if garmin data matters to you, or you want the optional online help with broader questions and meals. you do not need power to speak to the coach or to use the everyday commands in this guide. related free-form questions with power online ai help garmin data privacy: what stays where

title: Log food by talking or typing
summary: Tell the coach what you ate without opening a food form first.
text: the quickest way to log food is to tell the coach. speak when that is convenient, or type the same words on the coach screen. start with the meal and food say or type log breakfast 107 g cucumber . this gives the coach three useful pieces of information: that you are logging food, which meal it belongs to, and how much you had. use the amount you know. you do not need to turn your meal into a long description. log a drink say log espresso when that is all you need to record. small items can be logged in the same conversation as larger meals. there is no need to open a separate drinks screen. log another item keep going as you eat through the day. each request can be short. log my creatine is there for your supplement record too. open fuel from the grid menu at the top right when you want to review your food and targets in the full view. with forma power power adds optional online ai help for meal ideas, meal photos and meal descriptions. it is opt-in. you do not need power for the everyday coach requests on this page. speech recognition happens on your iphone and is never sent anywhere. tip: if speech is inconvenient in a public place, type the same request instead. the coach works either way. related meals, snacks and drinks your calorie and protein targets online ai help voice and privacy

title: Meals, snacks and drinks
summary: Keep everyday food logging short and natural.
text: you do not need a different workflow for every kind of food. tell the coach what you had and include the meal or amount when it helps. breakfast use a direct request such as log breakfast 107 g cucumber . naming the meal makes your intention clear. naming the amount adds useful detail when you know it. other meals and snacks use the same coach screen later in the day. say or type what you ate in the same plain way. you do not have to save a special meal template or remember a command for each food. start with the food itself. drinks a short log espresso is enough to begin logging that drink. coffee, water breaks and snacks do not require you to open fuel first. the full fuel view is there under the grid menu when you want it. when you want meal help with forma power, optional online ai help can provide meal ideas and help with meal photos and descriptions. you choose whether to turn it on. core still lets you talk or type to the coach and keeps everything on your phone. related log food by talking or typing keep food logging simple online ai help

title: Keep food logging simple
summary: Log as you go and use Fuel when you want to review the day.
text: food logging works best when it fits the meal you are having. a short request while it is fresh is easier than rebuilding the whole day later. log as you go tell the coach after breakfast, lunch, dinner or a snack. use simple requests such as log breakfast 107 g cucumber and log espresso . you do not need to wait until every part of the day is complete. review the day in fuel open the grid menu at the top right and choose fuel . this is the full food view when you want to look beyond the conversation. compare what is there with what you actually ate. pay particular attention to amounts, because a food name alone does not describe the portion. check your targets the first-run conversation reveals your starting calorie and protein targets. later, ask why is my calorie target what it is when you want an explanation. the protein number in the home strip gives you a quick reference. tap it for its chart. do not chase perfection a food log is information for you and your coach. it does not need to be a perfect record of every gram to be useful. ask am i on track or how was my week for a wider view instead of judging one meal on its own. related log food by talking or typing your calorie and protein targets your week

title: Your calorie and protein targets
summary: Where the starting targets come from and how to ask about them.
text: your first conversation with forma ends with a reveal of your calorie and protein targets. your first session appears with them. the answers behind the starting plan during setup, the coach asks about your goal, height, weight, sex, birth date, training days and where you train. those answers give forma the context for your starting targets. check that your answers reflect you, especially the body details and goal. ask why when you want an explanation, say or type why is my calorie target what it is . this is usually easier than trying to reverse-engineer the number from a chart. ask the question on the coach screen whenever the target surprises you. see protein at a glance protein is one of the six numbers in the quiet home strip. tap it to open its chart. for the full food and target view, open fuel from the grid menu. use targets as information a target is an estimate, not a medical prescription. your logged food, weight and other records help you look at what happens over time. ask am i on track for a direct check, or how was my week for a wider review. note: forma gives information, not medical advice. talk to a qualified professional before making major changes to how you eat if you have a medical condition or other health concern. related setting up weight and body trends your week

title: Your week
summary: Ask how the week went and whether you are on track.
text: a weekly review can be one question. on the coach screen, say or type how was my week . ask the question you actually have use a broad request when you want a summary: how was my week am i on track any patterns use a narrower request when one number matters: show my training volume how did i sleep this week show my bench progress you can follow a quiet week with the same questions. just remember that less logging means less information for the coach to use. open reports open reports from the grid menu at the top right. it starts with a short coach summary. below that, the on-track card brings together your fitness score, weight, muscle progress and body trends. choose full report to open the full progress screen. use more than one signal food and protein matter, but they are not the whole week. training, weight, sleep, hrv and resting heart rate can add context. the six home numbers give you a quick view. tap one for its chart, then return to the coach with a question if you want help reading it. tip: treat the weekly review as information for next week, not a grade for last week. related reports and the numbers on your home screen coach summaries, patterns and experiments your calorie and protein targets

title: Supplements
summary: Log what you take without turning Forma into medical advice.
text: you can log a supplement from the same coach screen as your food. say or type log my creatine . keep it simple tell the coach when you take it. you do not need to open fuel first. if you also want to log a drink such as coffee, use a separate short request like log espresso . review your day open fuel from the grid menu when you want the fuller view of your food and targets. the home-number strip includes protein. tap it for its chart when you want to see more than today's number. forma does not prescribe supplements logging creatine or another supplement is a record of what you chose to take. it is not a recommendation that you should take it, or how much you should take. ask a doctor, pharmacist or another qualified professional about supplements, interactions and your own health. forma gives information, not medical advice. related log food by talking or typing your calorie and protein targets about, and not medical advice

title: Start a training session
summary: Begin from the coach and add the context that matters today.
text: when you are ready, say or type start training on the coach screen. you do not need to find a separate start screen first. you can also open train from the grid menu at the top right. your first session the first-run conversation ends by revealing your first session, along with your calorie and protein targets. start with that session when you are ready. your setup answers about training days and where you train give forma its starting context. before you begin tell the coach anything that changes today: i only have 35 minutes equipment taken? warm up short context is enough. you do not need to write a long explanation. during and after training keep the coach close for what you need. ask about equipment, use train for the training view, and ask for cool down when you finish. later, you can ask show my bench progress , any new records or show my training volume to look back on the work you logged. careful: stop if something hurts or feels wrong. forma gives information, not medical advice. related short on time when equipment is taken mobility and stretching training history, records and volume

title: Warm up, train and cool down
summary: Use three short requests around your session.
text: a session can have a simple beginning, middle and end. ask the coach for the part you need instead of searching through menus. warm up say or type warm up before you train. use the warm-up to ease into movement and pay attention to how you feel. it is not a test of how hard you can go. train say start training when you are ready for the session. open train from the grid menu if you prefer the full training view. if the day is not going to plan, tell the coach. i only have 35 minutes and equipment taken? are useful starting points. cool down say cool down after the work is done. you can also ask for stretch when you want a gentler finish. there is no need to rush this part. give yourself a moment before heading back to the rest of the day. keep it comfortable a warm-up or cool-down should not be used to push through pain. stop if something feels wrong and speak to a qualified professional about an injury or symptoms. related start a training session mobility and stretching pain, illness and training

title: Mobility and stretching
summary: Ask for a warm-up, cool-down, desk reset or stretch.
text: you can ask the coach for a small amount of movement without starting a full training session. use the same coach screen by voice or text. before training say warm up when you want to prepare for your session. notice how your body feels as you move. a warm-up is a chance to ease in, not a demand to push harder. after training say cool down when the session is finished. ask for stretch if you want a quieter finish. you do not need to rush from your last movement straight back into a busy day. during a desk-bound day say desk reset when you have been sitting and want a short break. it can be a small pause even when a full session does not fit. you can also ask for stretch on its own. keep it comfortable and work within what feels right for you. keep the request in context use start training for a session and these shorter requests for the movement around it. on a busy day, telling the coach i only have 35 minutes adds useful context too. careful: stretching and mobility work are not treatment for an injury. stop if anything hurts and ask a qualified professional for advice. related warm up, train and cool down short on time pain, illness and training

title: Short on time
summary: Tell the coach how long you have and keep the day realistic.
text: you do not need to pretend a busy day is a normal one. before training, say or type i only have 35 minutes . use the real amount of time you have. the coach conversation is the place to add that context. a simple short-on-time routine tell the coach your time limit. say start training when you are ready. ask equipment taken? if a busy space gets in the way. leave a moment for cool down if you can. open train from the grid menu if you prefer the full training view. when a session will not fit a small movement break is still a useful choice for the day. ask for desk reset or stretch instead of forcing a full session into too little time. if the whole week is crowded, tell the coach it is a busy week. that is one of the few things it can remember on your phone. when you are back on track there is no catch-up punishment. return with start training , or ask how was my week when you want to review what happened. tip: keep your request specific. a real time limit is more useful than saying only that you are busy. related start a training session mobility and stretching training when your week changes

title: When equipment is taken
summary: Ask the coach what to do when your planned spot is busy.
text: a busy gym does not have to end the session. when the equipment you expected to use is occupied, ask the coach equipment taken? . ask while you are there use the coach screen on your phone. you can speak if your hands are full, or type if the gym is loud. give the coach the context it asks for. keep the request about what is available to you right now. use what you know about your training space the first-run conversation asks where you train. that gives forma a starting point before today's equipment problem comes up. if you train somewhere different while travelling, tell the coach. travel is one of the few pieces of context it can remember on your phone. choose a sensible alternative an alternative should fit your body as well as your surroundings. do not force a movement that hurts just to keep a session going. forma gives information, not medical advice. ask a qualified professional about training with an injury. related start a training session training where you are training when your week changes

title: Training where you are
summary: Your training location is part of your first conversation.
text: forma asks where you train during the first-run conversation. this helps the coach begin with your real setting rather than an imaginary gym. answer for your normal week choose the place you expect to use most often. think about the equipment and space you can actually reach, not an ideal setup you rarely use. your answer about training days matters too. a realistic week and a realistic place give the coach a useful starting point. when the setting changes tell the coach when you are travelling or when planned equipment is taken. these can be short messages, not a new setup routine. try equipment taken? when something is occupied. tell the coach you are travelling when the whole training setting has changed. when space and time are limited say i only have 35 minutes when time is the main constraint. for a small movement break, ask for desk reset or stretch . these requests start from the same coach screen as a full training session. related when equipment is taken short on time mobility and stretching

title: Training when your week changes
summary: Give the coach context about illness, travel and busy days.
text: not every week looks like the plan. tell the coach what is happening in a few words. you do not need to rebuild everything yourself. being sick tell the coach that you are sick when it affects your day. this is one of the few things the coach can remember on your phone. rest and medical decisions are bigger than an app. forma gives information, not medical advice. speak to a qualified health professional when you need care. travelling tell the coach that you are travelling. your first-run answers say where you normally train, but real weeks can be different. use the coach screen to ask for training or a small movement break that fits the day. stretch and desk reset are simple options when a full session is not realistic. a busy week tell the coach that it is a busy week. on a particular day, add something concrete such as i only have 35 minutes . a shorter session or a small amount of movement can be easier to fit in than an all-or-nothing plan. check the memories later open settings > data & backup > what the coach remembers to see or delete saved context about being sick, travelling or a busy week. related short on time what your coach remembers pain, illness and training

title: Training history, records and volume
summary: Ask what your training looks like over time.
text: training progress is easier to see over several sessions than in one hard day. ask the coach when you want the longer view. follow one lift say show my bench progress to look at bench. you can ask about another lift by using its name. look for the direction over time. one session can be affected by sleep, stress, equipment and many other ordinary things. check for records ask any new records after training or during a weekly review. a record is worth noticing, but it does not have to be the goal of every session. weeks with no new record still add to your history. look at training volume ask show my training volume when you want a view of the work you have done. volume is one part of the picture. read it alongside how you feel, your recovery numbers and your other progress reports. use reports for the wider picture open reports from the grid menu. the on-track card includes muscle progress alongside your fitness score, weight and body trends. choose full report for the full progress screen. note: trends need history. early on, the coach may have only a little to show. related strength reports and the numbers on your home screen how was your week

title: Understand your bench progress
summary: Ask for one lift's trend and read it in context.
text: to check bench, say or type show my bench progress . the coach gives you a direct way to ask without looking through every report. give the trend time to form one session is one point. more sessions make it easier to see whether your training is moving in the direction you want. try not to judge the whole trend from your best or worst day. look at the wider run of training. add context from the rest of forma you can read a lift trend beside other information: any new records for recent records; show my training volume for the amount of training; how did i sleep this week for sleep; how was my week for a broader review. the home-number strip also keeps this week, sleep, hrv and resting heart rate close by. tap one for its chart. when progress feels stuck a flat patch is information, not failure. sleep, a busy week, travel and illness can all coincide with a change in training. you can tell the coach about being sick, travelling or a busy week. ask any patterns when you want to explore the information forma has. note: pain is different from an ordinary plateau. stop if something hurts and seek qualified advice. related training history, records and volume strength coach summaries, patterns and experiments

title: Pain, illness and training
summary: Give the coach context without treating it as medical care.
text: tell the coach when you are sick or when life is affecting training. it can remember being sick on your phone, along with a few other kinds of context. what the coach can do you can tell the coach about being sick, travelling or a busy week and see those memories later. you can also ask for information about your logs, recovery numbers and training. that does not make forma a medical service. it does not diagnose an injury or decide whether it is safe for you to train. when something hurts stop if a movement hurts or feels wrong. do not use a warm-up, stretch, shorter session or equipment change to push through pain. talk to a doctor, physiotherapist or another qualified professional about symptoms and returning to training. in an emergency, contact your local emergency service. when you are sick give yourself room to make a careful decision. the coach can hold the context, but medical advice needs a qualified person who understands your situation. when you are ready to look at your routine again, how was my week and am i on track are gentle places to start. review what is remembered open settings > data & backup > what the coach remembers . you can see and delete the memory there. related what your coach remembers about, and not medical advice training when your week changes

title: Reports and the numbers on your home screen
summary: Use six quiet numbers for a glance and Reports for the fuller story.
text: forma gives you two levels of detail. the home screen keeps six numbers close. reports gives you a coach summary and the wider picture. the six home numbers the quiet strip on your home screen shows: this week for a quick weekly reference. protein for your protein number. weight for your weight record. sleep for your sleep information. hrv for heart-rate variability. resting heart rate for that recovery number. tap any one of the six to open its chart. you do not need to open reports first. ask instead of tapping the coach can answer direct questions about the same part of your life. try: how did i sleep this week resting heart rate this month show my body fat show my training volume use the coach when you want words and context. use a chart when you want to see the shape over time. open reports open the grid menu at the top right of the coach screen. choose reports . read the short coach summary first. look at your on-track card below it. the on-track card brings together your fitness score , weight , muscle progress and body trends . open the full progress screen choose full report in reports. this opens the full progress screen for a deeper look. reports and the home numbers are different views, not different records. use whichever level of detail suits the moment. note: numbers and scores are estimates and need context. forma gives information, not medical advice. related the fitness score weight and body trends recovery and sleep numbers your week

title: Weight and body trends
summary: Log a weigh-in by voice or text, then look beyond one day.
text: to record your weight, say or type i weigh 78.4 on the coach screen. use the reading from your scale and your usual unit. a single reading is a snapshot body weight can move for ordinary reasons that have little to do with your longer-term goal. try not to turn one morning into a verdict. give yourself enough time to build a record. a trend is more useful than reacting to every individual reading. find the weight chart weight is one of the six quiet numbers on the home screen. tap it to open its chart. you can also open reports from the grid menu. weight appears on the on-track card beside your fitness score, muscle progress and body trends. keep the context close your goal and food targets are part of the same picture. ask why is my calorie target what it is when a target needs explaining. for a wider review, ask am i on track or how was my week . these questions are more useful than treating weight as a daily pass or fail. optional apple health apple health can be used as an optional, read-only source. forma never writes to apple health. if you use a watch or health data, nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. note: speak to a qualified professional about unexpected or concerning weight changes. forma gives information, not medical advice. related reports and the numbers on your home screen your calorie and protein targets apple health

title: Body fat and muscle progress
summary: Ask about body composition and read it alongside other trends.
text: to ask about body fat, say or type show my body fat on the coach screen. reports also places muscle progress and body trends on your on-track card. this keeps them beside your fitness score and weight rather than treating one measurement as the whole story. look at direction, not just a number body-composition readings can vary. the method, device and conditions can all affect what you see. use the same source consistently where you can, and give the trend time to develop. avoid drawing a big conclusion from one reading. add training context muscle progress is easier to think about alongside training. ask: show my bench progress any new records show my training volume these are different views. a change in one does not automatically explain a change in another. optional connected data apple health is optional and read-only. forma power can add garmin data. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service, including when optional online ai help is on. note: body-composition information is an estimate, not a diagnosis. forma gives information, not medical advice. related reports and the numbers on your home screen weight and body trends strength

title: Strength
summary: Follow a lift, check records and look at training volume.
text: the coach gives you three direct ways to look at strength and training: a lift's progress, new records and training volume. follow a lift say or type show my bench progress . you can use the name of another lift when that is the one you want to see. give the chart enough history to show a direction rather than judging one isolated session. check new records ask any new records after a session or as part of your weekly review. records can be encouraging, but ordinary training without a record still counts. recovery, sleep and life outside training can all add context to a quieter patch. check training volume ask show my training volume for a view of the work you have logged. volume does not tell you everything about quality or recovery. read it with your coach summary, morning check-ins and recovery numbers when they are available. see muscle progress in reports open reports from the grid menu. the on-track card includes muscle progress, along with your fitness score, weight and body trends. choose full report for the full progress screen. tip: use how was my week when you want these separate training numbers brought back into a broader conversation. related understand your bench progress training history, records and volume reports and the numbers on your home screen

title: Recovery and sleep numbers
summary: Read sleep, HRV and resting heart rate without chasing one perfect night.
text: sleep, hrv and resting heart rate are three of the six quiet numbers on your home screen. tap any one to open its chart. sleep ask how did i sleep this week for a week-level view. a week is often more useful to review than a single night. look at the information alongside how you felt in your morning check-ins. hrv hrv means heart-rate variability. it appears in the home strip with the other recovery numbers. tap hrv for its chart. read it as one piece of information rather than a complete readiness diagnosis. resting heart rate ask resting heart rate this month when you want the monthly view. you can also tap resting heart rate in the home strip for its chart. the longer view can help you avoid overreacting to one reading. where readings can come from apple health is optional and read-only. forma power adds garmin data. you can say sync my watch when you want the coach to start a watch sync. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. careful: seek qualified medical advice about symptoms or readings that concern you. forma gives information, not medical advice. related reports and the numbers on your home screen morning check-in and nudges apple health garmin data

title: The fitness score
summary: Find the score on your on-track card and keep it in context.
text: your fitness score appears on the on-track card in reports. it sits beside weight, muscle progress and body trends so you can read it as part of a wider picture. find the score open the grid menu at the top right of the coach screen. choose reports . read the short coach summary. find the fitness score on your on-track card. choose full report when you want to open the full progress screen. use it as a summary the score is one way to look at your information. it is not the only measure of a good week, and it is not a medical test. read it beside the things you can observe directly: your training, food record, weight, check-ins and recovery numbers. ask the coach about the wider picture try am i on track for a direct question about your goal. ask how was my week for a broader review, or any patterns when you want to explore what forma has recorded. if you want more detail about one area, ask a narrower question such as show my training volume or how did i sleep this week . note: forma gives information and estimates, not medical advice. a score cannot diagnose your health or fitness. related reports and the numbers on your home screen your week coach summaries, patterns and experiments

title: Talk to your coach
summary: A grouped cheat sheet of useful things to say or type.
text: open forma and use the coach screen. speak or type in plain words. you do not need to open train, fuel or reports first. these examples are starting points, not special commands you have to memorise. log food, supplements and weight log breakfast 107 g cucumber log espresso log my creatine i weigh 78.4 include the food and amount when you know them. open fuel from the grid menu when you want the full food view. train and adapt the session start training i only have 35 minutes equipment taken? warm up cool down tell the coach about your time or equipment before you start when you can. move and loosen up desk reset stretch warm up cool down stop if anything hurts. forma gives information, not medical advice. ask about recovery how did i sleep this week resting heart rate this month you can also tap sleep, hrv or resting heart rate in the home-number strip to open a chart. ask about training progress show my bench progress any new records show my training volume use the name of the lift you want to check. trends become more useful as you build a history. ask about your body and targets show my body fat why is my calorie target what it is am i on track reports brings your fitness score, weight, muscle progress and body trends together on the on-track card. look for the wider picture any patterns run an experiment how was my week start with a question you care about. an experiment is a way to look at your own information, not a medical test. ask about the coach and your devices what do you know about me what can you do sync my watch to review or remove saved coach memories, open settings , then data & backup , then what the coach remembers . when you want more open-ended help forma power adds online ai help for free-form questions and meal ideas. it can also help with meal photos and descriptions. this help is opt-in. everyday coaching still works on your phone with core. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. related voice and privacy what your coach remembers core and power

title: One coach, many kinds of help
summary: Training, food, recovery and progress through one conversation.
text: forma has one coach screen. you do not have to decide which coach to open or which part of the app should answer. ask about training, then log breakfast, then check your sleep. the same conversation is the way in. one place to ask start with what you want to do: start training for a session; log espresso for food and drink; i weigh 78.4 for a weigh-in; how did i sleep this week for recovery; am i on track for the wider picture. the coach can also explain itself. ask what can you do if you are not sure where to begin. full screens when you want them the conversation does not replace every chart or log. open the grid menu at the top right and choose: train for training; fuel for food and targets; reports for the coach summary and progress. in reports, full report opens the full progress screen. information that works together a question can be about more than one part of your routine. you might ask any patterns after a busy week, or how was my week after logging food, training and check-ins. the answer can only use information forma has. a quiet week of logging means less for the coach to work with. a coach, not a clinician forma gives information and suggestions, not medical advice. it does not diagnose symptoms or replace a qualified health professional. related talk to your coach one coach, one menu reports and the numbers on your home screen

title: Morning check-in and nudges
summary: Tell the coach how you feel and choose a gentle start to the day.
text: the morning check-in is a quick way to tell forma how you feel. it takes a word or a number. you do not need to write a journal entry. check in with a word choose the one that fits best: wrecked flat normal good strong there is no best answer. a low-energy morning is useful information too. check in with a number you can say or type i feel 7 . use the number that matches your morning rather than the number you think you should choose. if you do not want to check in, you can carry on with something else. log breakfast, look at the home numbers, or close the app. the optional morning nudge forma can give you an optional morning nudge. it is a gentle prompt, not another task list. turn it on if a small morning cue helps you. leave it off if you prefer a quiet phone. the check-in and the nudge are separate choices: you can check in without wanting a notification. look at the day afterwards the home strip shows six quiet numbers: this week, protein, weight, sleep, hrv and resting heart rate. tap any one for its chart. you can also ask the coach how did i sleep this week or am i on track when you want more than the numbers. tip: if the nudge does not arrive, check that it is enabled and that ios is allowed to send forma notifications. focus modes can also hold notifications back. related a day with forma reports and the numbers on your home screen troubleshooting

title: Coach summaries, patterns and experiments
summary: Ask for the wider picture instead of reading every chart.
text: sometimes one number is enough. sometimes you want to know what the last few days mean. the coach can help you step back. start with your week ask how was my week . use it after you have logged some meals, training, check-ins or weigh-ins. for a direct check against your goal, ask am i on track . reports also opens with a short coach summary followed by your on-track card. ask about patterns try any patterns when you want the coach to look across the information it has. patterns are clues, not proof. a change in sleep, food or training can happen at the same time without one causing the other. more complete logging gives the coach more to work with. run an experiment ask run an experiment when you want to explore a change in your own routine. keep the question modest and observable. give it enough time to produce useful information. do not use an experiment to test symptoms, change medication, or push through pain. note: forma gives information, not medical advice. talk to a qualified health professional about medical decisions. choose the amount of detail use the coach screen for a short answer. open reports from the grid menu for the summary and your fitness score, weight, muscle progress and body trends. choose full report for the full progress screen. related reports and the numbers on your home screen the fitness score your week

title: Make the coach fit your life
summary: Use voice or text, add context and keep interruptions optional.
text: you do not have to use forma the same way every day. speak when your hands are busy. type when you want quiet. open a full screen only when you need it. add useful context tell the coach when something changes your normal routine. it can remember a few things you tell it, such as: a food you avoid; being sick; travelling; a busy week. these memories stay on the phone. you can see and delete them under settings > data & backup > what the coach remembers . choose how much guidance you want use a short request when you know exactly what you need, such as warm up or log espresso . ask a broader question when you want help understanding the day, such as am i on track or any patterns . the optional morning nudge is there if you like a prompt. you can leave it off and still use the morning check-in. keep the full screens close open the grid menu at the top right for train , fuel and reports . this is useful when you would rather browse than ask. there is no need to change coaches or rebuild your plan when your week changes. tell the coach what is happening and review the memories it keeps. related voice and privacy what your coach remembers morning check-in and nudges

title: What your coach remembers
summary: See and delete the few pieces of context kept on your phone.
text: the coach can remember a few things you tell it so you do not have to repeat them. these memories are stored on the phone only. what it may remember the coach can keep context such as: a food you avoid; being sick; travelling; a busy week. this is a small set of useful context, not a hidden biography. your ordinary requests and logs do not mean you have to give the coach more personal detail than you want to. ask what it knows on the coach screen, say or type what do you know about me . this is a quick way to start when you are curious about the information behind a response. see the memories yourself open settings . open data & backup . open what the coach remembers . you will see the memories the coach has kept. review them whenever you like. delete a memory use the delete option in what the coach remembers for anything you do not want the coach to keep. deleting a memory is separate from deleting all forma data. you can remove one piece of coach context without wiping your logs. note: these memories stay on the phone. they are not needed for online ai help, and nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. related privacy: what stays where voice and privacy export or delete all my data

title: Garmin data
summary: Forma Power can add Garmin information to your coaching.
text: forma power adds garmin data. it can give the coach more context alongside the training, food and check-ins you record. power and core core keeps the forma experience on your phone and does not include the garmin addition. power is the plan to choose if you want garmin data in forma. online ai help is a separate, opt-in part of power. sync your watch on the coach screen, say or type sync my watch when you want to start a sync. afterwards, you can look at relevant home numbers and charts. sleep, hrv and resting heart rate are all in the six-number strip. you can also ask how did i sleep this week or resting heart rate this month . other devices garmin is the first watch forma connects to directly. devices that save to apple health can share that way. more direct connections are planned. see other watches and rings . keep the numbers in context watch readings are one view of recovery. read them alongside your morning check-in and how your training actually feels. a number from a watch is not a diagnosis. speak to a qualified professional about symptoms or readings that concern you. the ai boundary nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. this remains true if you also opt into online ai help for free-form questions or meals. apple health is optional and read-only as well. forma never writes to apple health. related core and power recovery and sleep numbers apple health privacy: what stays where

title: Other watches and rings
summary: Garmin connects directly. Other devices can share through Apple Health. More are planned.
text: what works today garmin connects directly. it is part of forma power. see garmin data . anything that writes to apple health can share with forma through apple health. if your watch, ring or scale saves sleep, heart rate variability, resting heart rate, weight or activity to apple health, and you allow forma to read it, those numbers can appear in your home strip and charts. what arrives depends on what your device saves to apple health. see apple health . what is planned more direct connections are planned. there is no date and no promised list yet. forma does not need a watch. everything in core works without one. tell us what you use write to support@raveniq.ai and say which device you would like to see. it helps us decide what to add next. please do not send health data.

title: Online AI help
summary: Opt-in Power help for questions, meal ideas, photos and descriptions.
text: forma power adds optional online ai help. it can help with free-form questions, meal ideas, meal photos and meal descriptions. it is opt-in. forma core keeps everything on your phone and does not require this online help. what you can use it for free-form questions ask a broader question in your own words when you want online ai help with the wording or exploration. the everyday coach requests in this guide, such as log espresso and show my bench progress , still begin on the same coach screen. meal ideas ask for meal ideas when you want inspiration. treat them as ideas to consider, not a medical diet or a prescription. meal photos and descriptions use a meal photo or a written description when you want online ai help interpreting a meal. check the result against what you actually ate before relying on it. a photo can miss ingredients and portion details. a description can only use the detail you include. what is never sent from your watch nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. this applies to original watch information and anything forma derives from it. turning on online ai help does not change that boundary. voice and consent speech recognition stays on the iphone and is never sent anywhere. choosing to use an online free-form question or meal request does not change where speech recognition happens. if you do not want online ai help, leave it off and use core. you can still talk or type to the coach. note: ai meal estimates can be wrong. forma gives information, not medical advice. related free-form questions with power voice and privacy privacy: what stays where log food by talking or typing

title: Free-form questions with Power
summary: Optional online AI help for broader questions and meal ideas.
text: the coach screen is for everyone, not just power. core covers everyday coaching on your phone. forma power adds online ai help for free-form questions. start with everyday coaching with the coach screen, you can say or type requests such as: why is my calorie target what it is am i on track any patterns how was my week what can you do open the coach and ask in the same way whether you prefer voice or typing. what power adds power's optional online ai help supports broader free-form questions and meal ideas. it can also help with meal photos and descriptions. online ai help is opt-in. choose it only if you want that kind of help. using it is not a requirement for the everyday examples in this guide. watch data stays out of ai nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. this includes information forma worked out from watch data, not just the original readings. that boundary remains in place when you ask a free-form question with online ai help. speech remains on the iphone speech recognition happens on your iphone and is never sent anywhere. choosing online ai for a free-form request does not move speech recognition off the phone. note: forma gives information, not medical advice. do not use online answers as a substitute for professional care. related talk to your coach online ai help voice and privacy core and power

title: iCloud backup
summary: A backup in your own private iCloud, separate from online AI help.
text: forma's icloud backup uses your own private icloud. it is your apple account's backup space, not a public copy of your forma data. check your backup open settings , then data & backup , to find the backup controls and status. your iphone needs access to icloud for a backup to reach it. if the phone is offline, your on-device data is still there. what private icloud means the backup belongs to your own icloud account. forma core keeps everything on your phone, with this private backup rather than a forma cloud account for your daily logs. apple health remains optional and read-only. coach memories are stored on the phone. backup is not online ai backing up to your private icloud is separate from forma power's optional online ai help. online ai help is opt-in. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. before changing phones or deleting data check the backup status in settings > data & backup before making a major change. if you want a separate copy, use the export control in the same area. read deletion choices carefully so you know what will happen to the phone copy and the icloud backup. tip: do not send an export or health records to support unless you deliberately choose to share them. related export or delete all my data privacy: what stays where troubleshooting

title: Voice and privacy
summary: Speech stays on the iPhone, and the coach can read answers aloud.
text: you can speak to forma on the coach screen. speech is recognised on your iphone and is never sent anywhere. talk or type use voice when it is comfortable. type the same request when you are in a meeting, on a train, or anywhere you would rather stay quiet. for example, both ways work for requests such as: log espresso i weigh 78.4 start training how did i sleep this week you do not lose the coach-first experience by typing. listen to the coach the coach can read answers aloud. use this when listening is easier than reading. you remain in control of when to use voice and when to read silently. voice output does not change where your speech is recognised. what online ai changes forma core keeps everything on your phone. forma power adds optional online ai help for free-form questions, meal ideas, meal photos and meal descriptions. online ai help is opt-in. a free-form question or meal request you choose to send for online help is different from the speech recognition itself. your speech is still recognised on the iphone and is never sent anywhere. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. coach memories and backup the few things your coach remembers stay on the phone. see and delete them under settings > data & backup > what the coach remembers . icloud backup uses your own private icloud. export and delete controls are in settings. related talk to your coach what your coach remembers privacy: what stays where online ai help

title: Apple Health
summary: An optional, read-only source for your Forma numbers.
text: apple health is optional in forma. if you choose to connect it, forma reads from health. it never writes to health. read-only means read-only forma can use permitted health information without changing the records in apple health. your forma requests and logs do not get written back into health by the app. you can use forma without connecting apple health. talking to the coach, typing logs and using the main app do not depend on it. recovery and body numbers health data can add context to the numbers you already see in forma. the home strip includes weight, sleep, hrv and resting heart rate, and each opens a chart when tapped. you can also ask questions such as how did i sleep this week , resting heart rate this month and show my body fat . change your mind apple health access is your choice. you can review health permissions in apple's settings if you want to change what forma may read. removing access does not turn forma into a different app. you can continue to use the coach by speaking or typing. health data and ai nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. this remains true with forma power and optional online ai help. forma gives information, not medical advice. health readings are not a diagnosis. related recovery and sleep numbers privacy: what stays where garmin data

title: Export or delete all my data
summary: Find the data controls in Settings and choose what happens to your records.
text: forma puts export and deletion in settings. you can take a copy of your data or remove it without contacting support. export your data open settings . open data & backup . choose the export option. follow the iphone's sharing or saving flow. keep the export somewhere you trust. it can contain sensitive health, food and training information. delete all your data open settings . open data & backup . choose delete all my data . read the confirmation carefully before proceeding. deletion is a bigger step than removing one coach memory. use the memory controls if you only want to forget a food you avoid, being sick, travelling or a busy week. careful: export first if you want a copy. do not delete until you are sure you no longer need the data on this phone. icloud and apple health your icloud backup is your own private icloud copy. read the choices shown when you delete so you understand what happens to it. apple health keeps its own data and permissions. forma only reads from health and never writes to it. coach memories to remove only saved coach context, open settings > data & backup > what the coach remembers . you can see and delete those memories there without choosing delete all my data. related icloud backup what your coach remembers privacy: what stays where

title: Privacy: what stays where
summary: On-device coaching, private iCloud backup and clearly optional online help.
text: forma core keeps everything on your phone. optional features have different paths, so it helps to separate speech, memories, backup, watch data and online ai help. speech and typing speech is recognised on your iphone and is never sent anywhere. you can type instead whenever you prefer. the coach can read answers aloud. that does not require sending your speech away for recognition. coach memories the coach can remember a few things, including a food you avoid, being sick, travelling and a busy week. these memories stay on the phone only. see and delete them under settings > data & backup > what the coach remembers . icloud backup backup goes to your own private icloud. it is separate from optional online ai help. export and delete controls are in settings > data & backup . apple health and watch data apple health is optional and read-only. forma never writes to it. forma power adds garmin data. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service, even when online ai help is enabled. optional online ai help forma power can add online ai help for free-form questions, meal ideas, meal photos and meal descriptions. it is opt-in. only use it if you want those requests to use online ai. core provides the on-phone experience without it. a quick reference information or feature where it goes speech recognition on your iphone; never sent anywhere coach memories on your phone only core app data on your phone icloud backup your own private icloud apple health optional and read-only watch-derived information never sent to an ai service power online questions and meal requests online ai help, only when you opt in and use it related voice and privacy what your coach remembers core and power online ai help

title: About, and not medical advice
summary: What Forma's coach, targets and scores can and cannot tell you.
text: forma is a coach you talk to about training, food, recovery and progress. it gives information and suggestions, not medical advice. what the numbers are calorie and protein targets, charts, reports and the fitness score are based on the information available to forma. they can help you review your routine, but they are not diagnoses or prescriptions. the morning check-in records how you feel. it is not a clinical assessment. sleep, hrv, resting heart rate and body-composition information also need real-world context. what the coach is not forma is not a doctor, dietitian, physiotherapist or emergency service. it does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent a condition. logging creatine does not mean forma recommends it. asking for training, a warm-up or a stretch does not mean the app can decide whether an activity is safe for your body. talk to a qualified professional seek professional advice before changing how you eat or train when you have a medical condition, take medication, are pregnant, are recovering from an injury, or have concerns about food or your body. stop if something hurts or feels wrong. for urgent help, contact your local emergency service. experiments and patterns requests such as any patterns and run an experiment are ways to explore your own information. they do not prove cause and effect and should not be used to make medical decisions. note: you control your forma data. export and deletion are in settings, and coach memories can be reviewed under data & backup . related pain, illness and training privacy: what stays where export or delete all my data

title: When the coach does not understand
summary: Make a request clearer, type it instead, or see what Forma can do.
text: a request can be too broad, missing a detail, or hard to hear. you do not need to learn a special command language. a small clarification is usually the best next step. try a shorter request use one action at a time. these are reliable starting points: log breakfast 107 g cucumber log espresso log my creatine i weigh 78.4 start training how did i sleep this week include the food, amount, lift or period you mean when that detail matters. type instead speech is recognised on the iphone. if a noisy room makes speaking difficult, type the same words on the coach screen. typing is also useful when you want to check a number such as 78.4 before sending it. ask what forma can do say or type what can you do for help from inside the app. you can also use talk to your coach for a grouped cheat sheet of everyday requests. when you want a broader answer forma power adds optional online ai help for free-form questions. core still handles the everyday on-phone coaching described in this guide. do not add private medical details just to make a request clearer. forma gives information, not medical advice. related talk to your coach voice and privacy troubleshooting

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Simple checks for voice, nudges, watch sync, backup and surprising numbers.
text: start with the simplest check. most everyday requests can be typed if voice is not convenient, and your data controls are collected in settings. voice is not working well move somewhere quieter if you can. use a short request with one action, such as log espresso . type the same request on the coach screen instead. ask what can you do if you are unsure how to phrase it. speech recognition happens on the iphone and is never sent anywhere. typing does not change the privacy of that recognition. the coach is not reading aloud the coach can read answers aloud. check the iphone's volume and any audio output you are using, then try again. you can always read the answer silently. voice output is optional. the morning nudge does not arrive check that the optional morning nudge is enabled. then check that ios notifications for forma are allowed and that a focus mode is not holding them back. you can still use the morning check-in without the nudge. watch data looks old say or type sync my watch . then give the sync a chance to finish before checking the chart again. garmin data is part of forma power. apple health is optional and read-only. review the relevant device or health permission if you have changed it recently. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. icloud backup is not catching up open settings > data & backup and read the backup status. check that this iphone is signed in to icloud, has a connection, and has room for the backup. your on-device data remains separate from the private icloud copy. a target or chart looks wrong check the request or value you entered, especially decimal points and units. ask why is my calorie target what it is . review your goal and starting answers. tap the relevant home number for its chart, or open reports for the wider view. remember that targets, trends and the fitness score are estimates. forma gives information, not medical advice. online ai help is unavailable online ai help is part of forma power and is opt-in. check your plan and whether you have chosen to enable it. core's on-phone coaching is separate. you can continue to use everyday voice and typed requests without online ai help. related when the coach does not understand voice and privacy icloud backup core and power

title: Ways to log your food
summary: Speak, type, browse Fuel, or opt into meal help with Power.
text: use the method that fits the moment. the coach screen keeps the everyday choices simple, and fuel is under the grid menu when you want the full view. speak to the coach say what you ate, such as log breakfast 107 g cucumber or log espresso . speech is recognised on your iphone and is never sent anywhere. this is useful when your hands are busy and you can talk comfortably. type to the coach type the same request when you are somewhere quiet or want to check the wording and numbers first. there is no separate typed command language. the examples in the guide work as written requests too. open fuel open the grid menu at the top right and choose fuel . use it when you want to browse your food and targets rather than make a quick request. you can move between the coach and fuel as your needs change. the coach remains the main way into everyday logging. use optional meal help with power forma power adds opt-in online ai help for meal ideas, meal photos and meal descriptions. check meal estimates against the actual food and amount. photos and descriptions can miss details. nothing derived from your watch is ever sent to an ai service. method best for voice a quick log when you can speak typing quiet places and checking exact numbers fuel browsing the full food view power meal help optional ideas, photos and descriptions related log food by talking or typing voice and privacy online ai help

title: Ways to judge progress
summary: Glance at home numbers, ask the coach, or open the full report.
text: no single number has to carry the whole story. forma lets you choose a quick glance, a direct question or a fuller report. glance at the home strip the six numbers are this week, protein, weight, sleep, hrv and resting heart rate. tap one for its chart. this is useful when you want a quick check without starting a longer review. ask one clear question use the coach for the part you care about: show my bench progress any new records show my training volume how did i sleep this week resting heart rate this month show my body fat narrow questions make it easier to look at one trend without confusing it with another. read reports open reports from the grid menu. start with the short coach summary, then read the on-track card. the card includes your fitness score, weight, muscle progress and body trends. choose full report for the full progress screen. review the week ask how was my week , am i on track or any patterns when you want to step back. use more than one kind of evidence. food, training, weight and recovery can move differently. a pattern is a clue, not proof of cause. note: charts, targets and scores are estimates. forma gives information, not medical advice. related reports and the numbers on your home screen coach summaries, patterns and experiments strength

title: Ways to use training
summary: Start from the coach, browse Train, or ask for a smaller movement break.
text: training can begin with one spoken or typed request. the full train view and shorter movement options are close by when you want them. start with the coach say or type start training . before you begin, add context if the day needs it. i only have 35 minutes tells the coach your time limit. equipment taken? helps when your planned equipment is unavailable. open train open the grid menu at the top right and choose train when you prefer the full training view. the coach is still there when you want to ask about the session or your progress later. use movement around the session ask for warm up before training and cool down afterwards. stretch is another option when you want a gentler finish. these requests come from the same coach screen as start training . choose a small break instead when a full session does not fit, ask for desk reset or stretch . a short break can be a more realistic choice on a crowded day. tell the coach about being sick, travelling or a busy week when that context matters. you can review those memories later on your phone. careful: stop if something hurts. forma gives information, not medical advice. related start a training session short on time mobility and stretching

title: A lighter way to begin
summary: Build a useful routine without trying every feature at once.
text: you do not need to master forma in one week. start with the few actions that make the app feel useful, then add more when you want them. begin with one daily request pick the request you are most likely to remember: log espresso after a drink; i weigh 78.4 after a weigh-in; start training when it is time to train. speaking and typing both count. choose whichever feels less like work. add the morning check-in when you want to include it, choose wrecked, flat, normal, good or strong. you can also say i feel 7 . do not turn it into a test. a truthful normal or flat is more useful than an optimistic answer. learn where the full screens are open the grid menu at the top right. find train , fuel and reports once so you know where they are. then return to the coach. you do not need to browse those screens every day. end with a small review ask how was my week or tap one of the six home numbers for its chart. keep what worked. if daily logging felt like too much, make next week lighter rather than giving up on the whole routine. related your first week a day with forma morning check-in and nudges

title: A week focused on fat loss
summary: Use your targets and trends without judging single days.
text: if fat loss is your goal, begin with the targets forma revealed during setup. keep the week about useful information, not perfection. log the basics tell the coach what you eat with short requests such as log breakfast 107 g cucumber and log espresso . record weigh-ins with i weigh 78.4 , using your real reading and unit. protein is in the home-number strip when you want a quick glance. ask about the target say why is my calorie target what it is whenever the number needs explaining. your setup answers about your goal, body details and training week are part of the starting context. check them if something seems off. review more than the scale ask am i on track and how was my week . reports shows weight and body trends beside muscle progress and your fitness score. one weigh-in is a snapshot. training, food, recovery and the longer trend all add context. keep health ahead of the target do not use forma to push through illness, pain or symptoms. speak to a qualified professional before making major dietary changes if you have a medical condition, take medication, are pregnant, or have concerns about food or your body. forma gives information, not medical advice. related your calorie and protein targets weight and body trends about, and not medical advice

title: A week focused on building
summary: Bring food, training and recovery into one realistic review.
text: if your goal is to build, give the coach a realistic starting picture during setup. your training days, where you train and your body details all belong in that first conversation. start with the revealed plan at the end of setup, look at your calorie and protein targets and your first session. when you train, say start training . when you eat, use short requests such as log breakfast 107 g cucumber . protein is also one of the six home numbers. look at training over time ask show my bench progress , any new records and show my training volume as your history grows. one hard session is not the whole picture. a few weeks of consistent information are more useful than chasing a record every day. include recovery use the morning check-in when it helps. ask how did i sleep this week or tap sleep, hrv and resting heart rate for their charts. recovery numbers are information, not targets to perfect. read them alongside how you feel. review the whole week ask how was my week and am i on track . in reports, your on-track card includes muscle progress and body trends as well as weight and the fitness score. forma gives information, not medical advice. speak to a qualified professional about major changes to your diet or training when health concerns apply. related strength your calorie and protein targets reports and the numbers on your home screen
